solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old Bob drinks a lot, Marie too

parts.note: a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated S
to tope is to drink alcohol heavily, so he topes

explanation.surface: An old man called Bob is a heavy drinker, and so is a woman called Marie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bob' is not a person: a bob was a shilling in pre-decimal British money, written S. Marie Stopes was the British birth-control campaigner; 'too' just links her to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Stopes was the famous British pioneer of family planning, so the surname completes her first name.

clue.text: Work with female ending, early morning act

parts.note: toil means hard work
-ette is a suffix marking the feminine, as in usherette

explanation.surface: A woman finishes work as part of her early morning routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilette is the act of washing, dressing and grooming, usually done first thing in the morning.

clue.text: Learned person in old college taking single subject (American)

parts.note: a poly was a British polytechnic, a kind of college now mostly renamed universities
Americans say math, singular, where Britons say maths

explanation.surface: A scholar at an old college specialises in just one subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath is a person learned in many fields of study.

clue.text: European scruff, a man from Scotland?

parts.note: a sloven is an untidy, scruffy person
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Is that untidy European a Scotsman?
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovenian is a native of Slovenia, a country of Europe.

clue.text: A grim son, weird life form!

indicators.note: weird suggests something strange and out of shape, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a grim-faced son is a strange creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living thing, plant or animal, is a biological being of this kind, a synonym for a life form.

clue.text: Crazy characters in the madhouses, all very ancient

indicators.note: crazy means mad and disordered, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mad people in the asylums are all extremely old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in' says the letters of 'the madhouses, all' are what get rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the Bible's longest-lived man, so the phrase is an idiom for extremely old.

clue.text: Veronica not here? Look for someone else

indicators.note: look for asks us to search inside the words before for the answer's letters

explanation.surface: Veronica isn't here, so find somebody different.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means a different person, one more besides, someone else.

clue.text: Menial? Come to the conclusion one will want gold

parts.note: to infer is to come to a conclusion from evidence
I is the Roman numeral one
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A lowly worker decides he will want gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior means lower in rank or status, as a menial is.

clue.text: Tall building I look to go up in August?

indicators.note: in puts the reversed piece inside the month word

parts.note: August is a month

indicators.note: to go up in a down clue means the letters are read upward, backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Gazing at a skyscraper being erected in August.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to go up' means the piece is read upward, so backwards, before 'in' sets it inside the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A monolith is a single great block of stone, and by extension a massive tall structure.

clue.text: Calm water can make philosopher think without hesitation

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was the English philosopher

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the hesitation sound from the thinking word

parts.note: to ponder is to think something over
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Still water can help a thinker reflect without stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' signals dropping the hesitation sound; 'philosopher' is John Stuart Mill, not a generic thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A millpond is the still pool held behind a mill dam, proverbial for perfectly calm water.

clue.text: Technical expert with black box heading off

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the box word is cut away

parts.note: a coffin is the box a body is buried in

explanation.surface: A tech expert carries a black box from which the top has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' means the box word loses its first letter; the box is the burial kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert, especially one doing research.

clue.text: Appear 'lacking', as one might say, without a stitch on

indicators.note: as one might say tells us the words are spoken, and a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: appear means seem, and lacking means less, giving seem less

explanation.surface: Someone seems to be wanting, being completely naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a stitch on' looks like nudity but means made with no seam, without stitching.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment knitted in one piece has no join, so it is made with no stitched seam anywhere.

clue.text: What evensong may be in church — 'said'

parts.note: oral means spoken, said rather than written

explanation.surface: A remark about evensong in church being spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: Evensong is the Anglican evening service, often sung by a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is frequently sung by a choir, so it can be described as a choir-sung service.

clue.text: Line of verse is more banal, this writer admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: triter means more trite, more banal
this writer is the setter, meaning me

explanation.surface: The setter confesses that a line of poetry is rather banal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimeter is a line of verse with three metrical feet.

clue.text: Monstrous guise ogre conjured up

indicators.note: conjured up suggests magic transformation, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A terrible disguise is magicked up by an ogre.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means outstandingly bad, shocking or monstrous.

clue.text: Endless trouble with husband resulting from engagement

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the trouble word is dropped

parts.note: to be in a mess is to be in trouble

explanation.surface: Unending trouble with a husband follows on from getting engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts MESS to MES. 'engagement' is gears engaging, not a betrothal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth are said to mesh when they interlock, so the noun means their engagement.

clue.text: Highway east from Manchester City's old ground

indicators.note: east from means the E is taken away from the ground's name

parts.note: Maine Road was the stadium of Manchester City football club until 2003

explanation.surface: A highway runs east out of Manchester City's former football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Maine Road is the Manchester City football ground; 'from' removes the E, east, from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road is a principal highway.

clue.text: Ten hours, roughly, coming from (say) Hampshire

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or not neatly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journey from Hampshire takes about ten hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampshire lies in the south of England, so someone from there is from the south.

clue.text: Knowing only half the records

indicators.note: only half means just the front half of the records word is kept

explanation.surface: Someone is familiar with just half of the records.
explanation.walkthrough: Records are ARCHIVES; 'only half' keeps its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means knowing or roguish, as in an arch smile.

clue.text: Choosing commercial alternative

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
an option is an alternative

explanation.surface: Picking between an advert and something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Adopting a policy or plan means choosing to take it up.

clue.text: Attendant sure to run around after Charles

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the name
to run around means jumbled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A servant is certain to dash about after Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasseur was a uniformed attendant or footman in great houses and hotels.

clue.text: A new job daughter secured

parts.note: a chore is a routine job

explanation.surface: A daughter has landed a new job.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship anchored is held fast, so the word means made secure or fixed.

clue.text: Defence in a game good, leading to victory finally

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the word victory

explanation.surface: A defensive move in a game leads at last to victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence' is a formal justification, as in Plato's Apology of Socrates.
explanation.definitionFit: An apology in the old sense is a formal written defence of one's beliefs.

clue.text: Pink car being abandoned in the country

indicators.note: being abandoned means the car is left out of the flower word

parts.note: a pink is a flower of the same family as the carnation

explanation.surface: A pink car is left abandoned out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' is the flower, not the colour; 'being abandoned' removes CAR from CARNATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a country with its people, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Indicate what executive must do before letters can go out?

indicators.note: before places the signing ahead of the posting in the answer

parts.note: an executive must sign the letters
letters go out by post

explanation.surface: Office routine: the boss has to put a name to the letters before they are mailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost points the way, and figuratively to signpost something is to indicate it clearly.

clue.text: King giving gong to little man

parts.note: a gong is slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE
Ron is a short form of the man's name Ronald

explanation.surface: A monarch awards a medal to a small fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Honours bestowed with unseemly oiliness

indicators.note: unseemly means improper, out of proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Awards are handed out with improper greasy flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise someone is to treat them as a celebrity, which is to honour them.

clue.text: Conceited-looking fellow embraced by good-looking girl

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the fellow goes within the girl word

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
Andy is a typical man's name for a fellow

explanation.surface: A vain-looking man is held in the arms of an attractive girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a vain man fussy about dress, so dandyish means foppish and self-regarding in looks.

clue.text: In Oz, an extra source of heat — what it will do!

parts.note: the sun is the source of heat
the sun will dry things

explanation.surface: Down Under, an additional heat source, and what it does.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australian cricket an extra, a run not off the bat, is called a sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians call cricket extras, runs not scored off the bat, sundries.
